items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: we sent him and got Lee when Red Allen came in the band... We were on two trumpets... He stayed with us about three or four, about a month.

ctx.x: I mean, there was. I don't know, but I don't remember this one. Now, when I was with the big man in California, we played at Sam Sebastian's Cotton Club. They had two reviews, the color review and the white review for two months. Louie was in the phone, man. We recorded that. The skeleton in the closet. Yeah. And all that. And that's Shabby Willis-Ranger. She's got the closet. What the hell was a random. And we did a recording date there. For Decca, I think, or Columbia. It must have been Decca. Decca. And that…
That's a number that Lee Collins played when he came up to your club on the excursion. Remember? Mm-hmm. The saxophone player was telling us about Lee coming up there and playing that number.

Mm-hmm. I tell you, we sent him and got Lee when Red Allen came in the band, and Otis Jones. We were on two trumpets, you see. And we sent him and we got Lee. And Lee was, he could play good, but he couldn't read. And you had to read because the numbers were tight, you know. But for solos, Lee, yeah, he played. He played beautiful trumpet. But he couldn't read enough to stay with it. He stayed with us about three or four, about a month. He tried to break it. I mean, show him the parts, but he just didn't learn to…
